title: Three.js can support a much higher visual bar.
methodology: This is a curated twenty-project benchmark set prioritized for hgsim, not an official worldwide popularity ranking. It deliberately includes authored experiences, real-time world systems, authoring tools and appearance-ceiling renderers.

Every counted entry has primary-source Three.js evidence in code, package metadata or creator implementation documentation. Repository commits are pinned; activity dates do not imply every project first released in 2026. Historical studies are marked.

The current official gallery also includes custom renderers. Tidewater is excluded from the strict twenty because its present source uses its own WebGPU/WGSL engine. A gallery listing alone is not sufficient engine proof.

Live application hosts are outside this cloud network allowlist. Repository code, manifests, documentation and available creator captures were inspected; remote demos and hardware FPS were not independently benchmarked.

Author timing figures retain GPU, resolution, preset, reconstruction and measurement context. Progressive stills, captured splats, tiny composed scenes and logical instance counts are not moving-game frame-rate guarantees.
Code licensing and content licensing are recorded separately. Preview images are remote attributed research references, not hgsim assets or newly rendered screenshots.

Three r187 was released on 30 October 2026. Hgsim currently vendors r180 and GLSL onBeforeCompile patches; several modern WebGPU/TSL references require a deliberate migration. Better art, terrain, lit impostors and many atmosphere techniques can also be built on WebGL2.
conclusions: The current hgsim captures are below the demonstrated browser quality bar. Natural geology, dense canopy, lit aerial impostors and coherent atmosphere must become acceptance criteria.
Nanite Forest and Bruno Simon demonstrate rich navigable worlds. Their asset design, lighting, LOD and delivery pipelines matter more than copying headline triangle or tree counts.
Hgsim needs runtime-lit tree impostors with elevation views for overhead flight. Four side views with baked BasicMaterial lighting cannot provide the required canopy or near/far consistency.

A polished 60–90 second launch-to-landing corridor should precede world expansion. Test it in motion on a named hardware GPU at fixed resolution; retain SwiftShader as a compatibility regression check.

projects.name: Nanite Forest
projects.author: Victor Zakharov
projects.evidence: Source-verified Three.js forest with one million logical trees and 1.5 million bushes, GPU cluster LOD, hierarchical occlusion, lit impostors and temporal reconstruction.
capabilities: Three ^0.186.1 / TSL / indirect drawing
Albedo and normal impostors at four elevations from 0 to 90 degrees
Per-tree crossfades, wind motion vectors and shadow-specific culling
Author: RTX 4070 Ti, 1080p High, ground 3.50 ms GPU / 3.4M submitted triangles; canopy 7.04 ms / 7.5M triangles plus 34k impostors
projects.lesson: Use dense canopy masses, multiple species and forest-floor dressing as the vegetation bar. Replace side-only prelit cards with runtime-lit azimuth/elevation impostors before adding arbitrary tree counts.
projects.caveat: The billion/trillion headline counts are logical full-detail scene size, not triangles drawn each frame. Hardware figures are author measurements, not ours or a guarantee for hgsim.
projects.license: MIT code. Stanford Lucy asset is separately noncommercial; exclude it from reuse. Inspect individual assets.
projects.imageCaption: Author-published ground-level capture; reported RTX 4070 Ti setup. This is a reference project, not hgsim.

projects.name: Bruno Simon — Folio 2025
projects.author: Bruno Simon
projects.evidence: A playable authored vehicle world whose Three WebGPU source integrates terrain, foliage, water, wind, day/year cycles, weather, physics and audio.
capabilities: Three ^0.187.0, WebGPURenderer and RenderPipeline
Blender-authored assets, compressed GLBs and ETC1S/KTX2 textures
Shared weather/lighting state and quality-specific post-processing
projects.lesson: Treat the launch-to-landing corridor as a deliberately authored place. Coordinate assets, motion, lighting, sound and delivery instead of assembling unrelated effects.
projects.caveat: Stylized, compact vehicle world. Its polish does not establish a realistic 14 km flight world at an unspecified frame rate.
projects.license: Actual license.md is MIT; package metadata says ISC. Audit music and other third-party assets separately.
projects.imageCaption: Creator preview of the playable stylized world. It demonstrates integrated art direction rather than photorealism.

projects.name: Three Geospatial — Atmosphere and Clouds
projects.author: Takram Design Engineering
projects.evidence: Three.js atmosphere and cloud systems with aerial perspective, volumetric clouds, cloud shadows, temporal filtering and geospatial scenes.
capabilities: Precomputed atmospheric scattering and linked sun/sky/aerial perspective
Beer cloud shadow maps affecting scene objects
Historical author v0.0.1 Tokyo benchmark: iPad Pro M4 60 FPS Medium at 2420x1520 with upscaling; M3 Max 92–95 FPS High 4K with upscaling, 31 FPS without
projects.lesson: Make the sun, terrain light, distance extinction and cloud shadows one coherent system. A photographed sky remains a compatibility fallback.
projects.caveat: Cloud WebGPU migration is marked WIP; WebGPU atmosphere requires Three >=0.182. Published figures are historical author measurements. LFS previews could not be downloaded here.
projects.license: MIT code; map imagery, tiles and service terms are separate.

projects.name: Threejs-Punk
projects.author: Anderson Mancini and Sunag
projects.evidence: A walkable authored cyberpunk alley with wet PBR surfaces, planar reflections, GPU rain, roof-aware splashes, clouds, fog and BVH collision.
capabilities: Three ^0.185.1 and WebGPU renderer
5,000 rain instances; 512-square collision height target
Half-resolution AO, bloom and reflection budgets; split compilation and device gates
Draco/KTX2 assets and an integrated HDR/post-processing pipeline
projects.lesson: Give every expensive feature a scene purpose and an explicit budget. Model real locations and make effects interact correctly with roofs, surfaces and collision.
projects.caveat: A bounded night street is not an open daytime flight world. No independently reproduced FPS result; historical SSR was replaced by planar reflections.
projects.license: MIT code; public models, textures, audio and videos explicitly excluded from that grant.
projects.imageCaption: Creator preview of the 2026 walkable scene. Night lighting and a bounded environment are important qualifications.

projects.name: Procedural Terrains 2.0
projects.author: ZyFou
projects.evidence: Interactive terrain authoring plus a plain-Three runtime with erosion, imported elevation, biome materials, streaming, clipmaps, LOD morphing, clouds and water.
capabilities: Tile, infinite, planet and miniature modes
GPU height/normal/biome evaluation and collision-map export
Shared-border/geomorph strategies and terrain export to DCC tools
projects.lesson: Author erosion, drainage, cliffs and biome structure before surface polish. Evaluate export into a shared physical terrain source first.
projects.caveat: Its CPU heights approximate the GPU field, and shaders own lighting/display encoding. Direct insertion would break hgsim collision and tone-mapping contracts. Preview FPS is not our measurement.
projects.license: MIT code; audit imported geographic imagery/assets separately.
projects.imageCaption: Maintainer terrain-studio capture. The displayed hardware/FPS belongs to that capture, not an independent benchmark.

projects.name: Claude of Tanks
projects.author: Kevin Liu
projects.evidence: A Three.js combat game with authored outdoor environments, dense overlapping canopies, dressed roads/settlements and raymarched clouds with world-anchored shadows.
capabilities: Direct THREE.WebGLRenderer source
Volumetric cloud and shadow-cascade implementation
Terrain, vegetation and material stages in the world source
projects.lesson: Aim for coherent land use, canopy coverage, grounded undergrowth and atmospheric depth. Repeated isolated tree symbols are below this bar.
projects.caveat: Creator captures show richer stylized game art, not an independent whole-game performance result. Do not repeat inconsistent fleet counts as verified facts.
projects.license: Root MIT has proprietary exceptions for world, vehicles, media and other content; reference those assets rather than copying them.
projects.imageCaption: Creator-published stylized outdoor combat capture. Its world/media content has separate proprietary terms.

projects.name: EZ-Tree
projects.author: Dan Greenheck
projects.evidence: Three.Group-based procedural trees with adjustable bark, branch and leaf geometry, wind, consistent-skeleton LOD generation and PNG/GLB export.
capabilities: Shared bark/leaf materials across LODs
createGeometry(detail) for custom instancing systems
Authored presets and configurable leaf card count, size, variance and orientation
projects.lesson: Evaluate a proven tree-authoring foundation for fuller, varied crowns and a consistent LOD family. Judge silhouette, canopy mass and light response rather than needle-face totals.
projects.caveat: A tree generator does not solve whole-forest placement, aerial impostors, overdraw or scene performance. Exporting all LODs can include unnecessary meshes.
projects.license: MIT code and bundled leaves per texture notice; ambientCG bark is explicitly CC0. Retain those notices.

projects.name: Poseidon
projects.author: Owen Yuwono
projects.evidence: An interactive spectral ocean: GPU FFT, three wave cascades, persistent foam, dielectric water optics and camera-centered geometry to a distant horizon.
capabilities: JONSWAP/Horvath bands and Stockham compute FFT
Fresnel, subsurface scattering and coherent sun/sky haze
Per-frame simulation/render loop and a camera-centered radial grid
projects.lesson: Use coherent multi-scale silhouette, shading and motion for water and terrain. A lake or river can enrich the valley without adding an ocean solely for spectacle.
projects.caveat: WebGPU-only, no WebGL fallback. No comparable hardware/FPS table was found; the author capture is not a progressive path-traced still.
projects.license: MIT code; separately credited sky asset/custom CC0 terms.
projects.imageCaption: Author golden-hour ocean capture, 2400x1350; no independent frame-rate measurement.

projects.name: 3D Tiles Renderer — Three.js examples
projects.author: NASA AMMOS and contributors
projects.evidence: The Three-specific Mars, terrain and photorealistic-tile examples demonstrate hierarchical loading, error-based detail, tile fades, overlays and geospatial scene streaming.
capabilities: The selected example directly imports Three Scene and WebGLRenderer
Three, Babylon and PlayCanvas adapters are distinguished in the source
Tile cache, region loading and custom material/plugin paths
projects.lesson: Stream a carefully authored/geographic region with explicit residency and geometric error budgets rather than loading the entire world before flight.
projects.caveat: Rendering tiles does not automatically provide exact flight collision. Google/Cesium data may require keys, payment, attribution and provider-specific terms.
projects.license: Apache-2.0 code; terrain/photogrammetry data and service rights are independent.

projects.name: Quick Grass
projects.author: SimonDev
projects.evidence: A Three.js grass implementation with instanced near/far geometry, wind, player bending, curved blade normals and wrapped/back-scattered lighting.
capabilities: Six-segment near / one-segment far geometry, source cutoff 15 m
Ten-metre patches and a 100 m visibility envelope
Half-float offsets and coherent grass shading
projects.lesson: A meadow needs translucent-looking light, motion, patch density and stable distance transitions. More opaque blade triangles alone will not create that finish.
projects.caveat: An older technical study inspired by a GDC grass presentation, not shipped Ghost of Tsushima code or a 2026 production game. No verified target-device FPS.
projects.license: MIT repository code; independently review referenced textures.

projects.name: Henry Heffernan — computer-room portfolio
projects.author: Henry Heffernan
projects.evidence: A detailed authored computer room and functional monitor UI; source loads baked textures and constructs Three MeshBasicMaterial for the staged environment.
capabilities: Blender-authored room/props and baked illumination
Interactive monitor and separate functional inner-site system
Fine object placement, restrained palette and controlled camera staging
projects.lesson: Use authored geometry and appropriate baked lighting for static launch equipment and hero props. Detail and composition can outperform an expensive generic PBR surface.
projects.caveat: Baked light and a bounded room do not establish a freely moving day/night landscape. The source snapshot is older than 2026.
projects.license: LICENSE.md grants MIT; package metadata says UNLICENSED. Inspect any third-party model/art rights.
projects.imageCaption: Creator room preview; lighting is authored/baked rather than evidence of unrestricted dynamic GI.

projects.name: N8AO
projects.author: N8 Programs
projects.evidence: A mature contact-occlusion pipeline with temporal stability, half-resolution reconstruction, depth-aware upsampling, optional neural denoising and GPU timing support.
capabilities: Contact shadows across complex scene geometry
EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 timing support
Explicit quality and transparency tradeoffs
projects.lesson: Compare a maintained AO implementation against the bespoke pass, especially during low-flight camera motion and through cutout foliage.
projects.caveat: Screen-space visibility misses hidden/offscreen geometry; transparency can need extra work. Published speedups are maintainer estimates, not hgsim guarantees.
projects.license: README/LICENSE say CC0; package says ISC. Resolve metadata discrepancy before redistribution.

projects.name: Spark 2.4
projects.author: World Labs and Spark contributors
projects.evidence: Photographic Gaussian-splat scenes mixed with Three meshes, with editing, animation, camera-relative precision, paged/streamed LOD and large-scene tooling.
capabilities: Three WebGLRenderer plus SparkRenderer/SplatMesh source
LOD .RAD trees and residency budgets
Shader-graph color/displacement edits and skeletal animation
projects.lesson: Captured detail is a valid appearance reference and possibly a bounded background technique; pair it with deliberate collision, lighting and streaming design.
projects.caveat: Splats are not automatic collision geometry or a fully relightable physical terrain. The dynamic-lighting example uses SDF color edits; concentrated transparent overdraw is costly.
projects.license: MIT code; each captured scene retains separate data rights.

projects.name: three-gpu-pathtracer
projects.author: Garrett Johnson
projects.evidence: Physically based progressive rendering with area lights, indirect illumination, materials, depth of field, denoising and upscaling in current Three WebGPU.
capabilities: renderSample() progressively accumulates the image
Moving low-resolution preview and GPU-budget paths
Complex photoreal indoor/outdoor reference scenes
projects.lesson: Generate trustworthy lighting/material reference images and selected static bakes; use those to judge rock reflectance and cloth before tuning the flight renderer.
projects.caveat: A converged still is not a moving open-world 60 FPS result. Current API requires a renderer/version migration from hgsim r180.
projects.license: MIT code; example models/HDRs have their own licenses.
projects.imageCaption: Progressive path-traced reference image; it is deliberately not presented as proof of 60 FPS flight gameplay.

projects.name: THREE.js PathTracing Renderer
projects.author: Erich Loftis
projects.evidence: Interactive ray/path-traced outdoor demos with procedural terrain, ocean, physical sky/clouds, global illumination, reflections, caustics and volumetric effects.
capabilities: Direct Three imports and specialized fullscreen shaders
Raymarched/analytic geometry and light transport
Many outdoor and interior reference scenes
projects.lesson: Use physically coherent sky/water/indirect-light behavior as reference, while budgeting a practical raster/hybrid game renderer.
projects.caveat: Specialized scene representations and progressive convergence matter. Author broad frame-rate claims were not independently repeated here.
projects.license: CC0 code; check individual referenced model/image assets.

projects.name: Post Processing — HDR and Sponza demos
projects.author: Poimandres contributors
projects.evidence: A maintained Three effects framework demonstrating HalfFloat HDR buffers, consistent output color/tone mapping, grading, AO, bloom, DoF and merged passes.
capabilities: Automatic merging of compatible EffectPass effects
Single fullscreen triangle and linear/HDR workflow
Current peer range includes Three 0.180 through 0.187
projects.lesson: Adopt a consistent, measured final-image pipeline and consolidate effects rather than adding independent expensive passes.
projects.caveat: A renderer/effect demo cannot supply missing scene composition or production art. Example scenes/assets need separate credits.
projects.license: Zlib code; separate example-asset terms.

projects.name: realism-effects — SSGI and temporal rendering
projects.author: 0beqz
projects.evidence: Three-based screen-space GI, reflections, denoising, temporal reprojected antialiasing and motion blur show a substantially richer indirect-light pipeline.
capabilities: SSGI/SSR and temporal history
Reprojection/denoising and motion-vector-related effects
Source peer Three ^0.151.3
projects.lesson: Judge indirect light and temporal stability together, including disocclusion at cliff edges and foliage in fast banked flight.
projects.caveat: Older experimental code and incompatible peer range make this a visual/algorithm reference, not an unchecked dependency. Screen-space effects have visibility and ghosting limits. The linked demo is a v2 preview; the pinned evidence is historical main.
projects.license: MIT code; scene assets require separate review.

projects.name: PHY — terrain, grass and character demos
projects.author: lo-th and contributors
projects.evidence: Three and Three WebGPU scene renderers integrated with physics, HDR presentation, island terrain, wind-animated grass and character/vehicle demos.
capabilities: Explicit Three and three/webgpu imports
Terrain and grass demonstrations
Worker/direct physics integration across multiple engines
projects.lesson: Rich presentation and trustworthy physical surfaces can coexist. Keep the flight solver independent while replacing terrain and collision representations together.
projects.caveat: A toolkit/demo suite is not a finished open-world quality or frame-rate proof. Some engine integrations have separate source/license constraints.
projects.license: MIT repository; audit each physics engine and imported assets.

projects.name: Emerald Bayou
projects.author: Vheissu
projects.evidence: A large browser water/terrain game with worker-built quadtree terrain, consistent vegetation placement across LOD, reflection/refraction targets, weather and wakes.
capabilities: Three ^0.185.1 with direct terrain/water imports
Camera-centered chunk/worker residency
Author describes a roughly 25.6 km square world
projects.lesson: Study cell residency, stable vegetation anchoring and coherent shore/water interaction as world-systems references.
projects.caveat: A promising engineering project rather than an established photoreal leader. Large advertised area does not imply uniform high-detail coverage or verified FPS.
projects.license: MIT code; audit the separately shipped large GLB asset pack before reuse.

projects.name: Sketchbook
projects.author: Jakub Blaha / swift502
projects.evidence: A historical authored Three.js game world with character movement, cars, aircraft/helicopters, Cannon physics, ocean and cascaded sun shadows.
capabilities: Blender/GLB scene authoring and a real third-person controller
Three WebGLRenderer, ACES, FXAA and shadow composer
Aircraft gameplay inside an authored environment
projects.lesson: Use it as an earlier proven integration floor: vehicle gameplay and authored scenery can work together. The new hgsim target should exceed this old visual baseline.
projects.caveat: Explicitly archived and older than 2026. It is a historical comparison, not a newly released 2026 graphics leader or a current dependency recommendation.
projects.license: MIT repository; inspect scene and texture rights separately.

targets.current: Rounded/repeated landforms and flat-capped launch outcrops remain visually schematic despite photographic maps.
targets.target: Author one coherent launch escarpment and eroded valley with intentional ridgelines, exposed strata, believable ledges, talus and material transitions. Derive render and collision from the same assets; preserve touchdown accuracy before introducing new terrain LOD.

targets.current: Side-view prelit tree cards produce sparse dark repeated silhouettes and weak overhead canopy.
targets.target: Use multiple species/ages, canopy masses and ecological edges. Bake azimuth plus elevation albedo/normal views, light and shadow them at runtime, and crossfade mesh/impostor transitions.

targets.current: Fine grass exists, but the ground lacks continuous undergrowth, litter and coherent translucent foliage light.
targets.target: Create linked meadow/forest-floor kits with grass clumps, shrubs, ferns, litter and deadwood; shared wind, wrapped/back-scattered leaf lighting, density/LOD fading and grounded contact shadows.

targets.current: A photographic sky and uniform fog are insufficient to unify aerial scenery.
targets.target: Connect sun radiance, sky scattering, terrain light, distance extinction and cloud shadows. Prototype temporally reconstructed volumetrics with a tuned skybox fallback; avoid unstable low-quality fog/noise.

targets.current: Texture detail exceeds the underlying shape/composition of some launch elements.
targets.target: Art-direct the launch as a credible place with weathered structural detail, anchor hardware, footpaths and prop clusters. Judge geometry/silhouette and material response against physically lit or baked reference images. Preserve rig/bone and flight-force contracts.

targets.current: Fixed captures and a bespoke AO pass do not establish stable flight imagery.
targets.target: Require normal-speed launch, bank, canopy flyover, low pass and landing footage without obvious LOD pops, foliage shimmer, AO halos or tone-map discontinuities. Use a measured linear/HDR/temporal pipeline.

targets.current: The draft regresses in SwiftShader and eagerly loads a large asset pack; hardware GPU performance is unverified.
targets.target: Proposed acceptance: native 1920x1080, fixed High preset on an RTX 3060 desktop 12 GB reference GPU (proposed, not measured here), 60 FPS median and p95 <=20 ms over the same 60–90 second route after warm-up. Record GPU/CPU times, effective resolution and memory. Stream compressed GLB/KTX2 assets; no benchmark frame-rate is claimed yet.

targets.current: R180 GLSL patches and conservative analytic collision shapes constrain integration choices.
targets.target: Build a small independently measurable WebGPU/TSL prototype while retaining the working WebGL2 path. Choose features by measured visual gain and cost; transfer techniques/appropriately licensed content without assuming modern libraries are drop-ins.
